findings.title: Read-only receipt snapshots destructively finalize hashes and break every normal positive proof
findings.trigger: A normal receipt is proven by #proveDomainGone, which calls accumulator.state(); the success path next calls #receiptEligibility, which calls state() on the same three Hash objects again. inspectCleanup also invokes state before later segments/proof.
findings.impact: state uses Hash.digest rather than a non-consuming snapshot. Second digest throws ERR_CRYPTO_HASH_FINALIZED, and an earlier inspection also prevents later update(). The catch then invokes #fail -> #proveDomainGone -> state again, so the void #run can reject without settling the issued promise. Small normal ASCII protocol cannot complete even with perfect kernel/receipt behavior.
findings.contract: Private contract A inspectCleanup read-only and normal positive route; R3 SPEC3 segmented receipt and SPEC8 actual orchestration tests.
findings.minimalFix: Make state a non-mutating immutable snapshot (e.g. copy each hash before digest), preserve live accumulators for later segments, and prevent error-cleanup proof from throwing outside owned handoff.
findings.actualBranchMock: Feed real cacheInterpretControlMessage/CacheReceiptAccumulator, call state twice, inspect between segments, then validate domain and eligibility on the same accumulator; drive the supervisor returned-child/event branch to actual settlement. Current tests call state only once per newly created accumulator.
findings.futureDecisiveRuntime: After authorization, exact synthetic normal N roundtrip must return the expected buffer and permit repeated active/terminal inspect calls without altering seq/digests or settlement.

findings.title: The nofork pilot still declares cleanup complete after timeout and lacks asynchronous startup ownership
findings.trigger: Any nofork identity assertion/startup failure or delayed close enters endChild. Its fresh close listener may miss an already emitted close; it races 2/3/5s timers then returns void. terminated===true can never match a close promise resolving void. The case unconditionally sets pilot.settled=true. Direct spawn and channels have no error listeners.
findings.impact: It can mark cleanup successful without actual close, attempt a needless KILL after an observed close, or crash on asynchronous spawn/socket error. This is a genuine first-stage safety blocker before any AUTHORIZE_FORK. The positive pilot also has no cancel/reap finally: it merely inspects and may discard its registered owner via owned.splice while resources remain held.
findings.contract: R3 SPEC7: first identity pilot must safely fail, immediate child/close ownership, deadline never means ended, live owner/evidence retained.
findings.minimalFix: Register persistent error/exit/close facts at spawn, use an unambiguous close result, never signal a proven exited child, and set settled only after real nofork C close/reap. On timeout retain a live owned handle and report unknown, not return successful cleanup. For positive stage, bind supervisor+issued handle+actual child/domain owner into the registry and provide a real exact-owned cleanup/reconcile finally; never KILL a forked C as fallback.
findings.actualBranchMock: Returned fake ChildProcess emits close before cleanup, exit before delayed close, error with no PID, and delayed/no close; assert truthful terminal/unknown state and no post-exit signal attempts. Deliberately throw an assertion after birth. Stub the actual endChild ownership flow, not a separate boolean helper.
findings.futureDecisiveRuntime: First authorized case sends no AUTHORIZE_FORK, intentionally fails an assertion after HELLO, and still records exact C epoch/exit/close before ending; unknown must preserve owner/output. Positive-N cleanup is a separate later case.

findings.title: Resource-ended proof still rejects legitimate failed startup and cannot reconcile preHELLO failures
findings.trigger: N exec fails with a real errno or setsid fails: C retains/reaps N and emits an outcome=reaped receipt with exec.ok=false. Host domain validator requires successful exec whenever forked_pid is non-null, so cleanup is held despite actual ECHILD/group gone. reconcile then rejects facts.worker===null. Separately asynchronous spawn-no-child emits error/close but no exit; custodianBorn is written but never used by the proof, which requires custodianExit.
findings.impact: Normal infrastructure failure cannot return its original failure after complete cleanup; PRE/scope/run directory stay held permanently with no live C to obtain a different receipt. Installed error listeners prevent a Host crash but do not close the no-birth lifecycle.
findings.contract: R3 SPEC2 explicitly separates raw execution-ended from result-success; SPEC1/4 preHELLO and asynchronous error branches must finish or retain real unknown responsibility.
findings.minimalFix: Model no-birth, failed setup/exec and successful exec as distinct authenticated fork outcomes. Accept complete raw cleanup for a failed exec while refusing picture eligibility; allow reconcile using retained C/fork identity before N_HELLO. For verified no-child spawn error+actual close, do not require an exit event that Node does not emit; never treat arbitrary error as no-birth.
findings.actualBranchMock: Drive actual returned ChildProcess error/close-without-exit and actual supervisor FORKED exec-failure message flow. Domain cleanup succeeds as a failed result with original errno; business eligibility remains false. Test preHELLO C death remains held.
findings.futureDecisiveRuntime: After positive baseline, authorized missing-worker exec, setsid failure and no-child spawn-error cases must actually reap/close and release once with original error, alongside C-dies-after-fork failclosed control.

findings.title: Unknown N identity can skip escalation and make a live TERM-ignore domain unrecoverable
findings.trigger: After controlled fork, C's exec/settlement identity reads are unknown so worker_identity is still None. _target_census only reads N when worker_identity exists and skips worker_pid in direct_children. Thus it can claim no live/unknown target despite live N; it goes straight to _reap_worker, times out without sending KILL. Recovery later sees a known TERM-ignoring N, but every _settle_domain(resignal=False) starts escalated and never sends any KILL.
findings.impact: C and anchor are retained (R3A expiry fix works), but the domain never actively ends after census readability recovers. This is permanent held substituting for the promised actionable cleanup, not a remaining60s exit. Existing adapter/recovery tests prepopulate worker_identity and miss this branch.
findings.contract: R3 SPEC1 unknown must be represented from actual fork authority, and ordinary TERM-ignore must complete via retained owned TERM/KILL/wait rather than permanent held.
findings.minimalFix: Always account for the unreaped forked N even before any accepted identity; unknown read must produce unknown census. Retain action/escalation state across recovery and permit the still-required exact-owned KILL after identity/authority becomes known, without resending blind group signals or losing N anchor.
findings.actualBranchMock: Use actual _settle_domain -> KernelSettlementOperations with worker_pid set but worker_identity=None, first reads unknown then known live, waitpid returns0 until a verified KILL. Assert N never reaped under uncertainty and eventual KILL/adopted waits/Nlast when readable; do not seed the fake with a ready zombie.
findings.futureDecisiveRuntime: Authorized preHELLO/late identity-read failure and restored readability, with actual TERM-ignore N, must complete and preserve peer; no repeated unsafe signals or responsibility deadline.

findings.title: Diagnostic accounting stops as soon as settlement begins
findings.trigger: After FINALIZE/CANCEL switches from _run_loop to TargetSettlement, N/descendants write stdout/stderr (e.g. TERM handler), then exit. KernelSettlementOperations.sleep only sleeps and _wait_for_recovery ignores stream events. There is no final stream drain before receipt.
findings.impact: Already detected overflow now latches correctly, but bytes emitted during settlement/recovery can remain unread and be omitted from stdout_bytes/stderr_bytes. A candidate can be eligible despite actual cumulative output exceeding64KiB; full diagnostics/FD-drained claims are unsupported by actual code. This is not a claim that elapsed cleanup proves settlement.
findings.contract: ADR F07 and R3 SPEC2/4 every-phase diagnostics budget and original failure preservation.
findings.minimalFix: Service bounded stream reads throughout settlement/recovery without starving wait/cancel, and prove stream EOF/final bounded drain after targets end before emitting counts. Read failures must be explicit unknown/lost diagnostics and disqualify success while permitting proven raw failure cleanup.
findings.actualBranchMock: Drive actual KernelSettlementOperations/Custodian phases with late stdout on TERM and total just over64KiB, then real-shaped waits; assert actual drain/latch/counts, not merely manually setting diagnostics_lost in validator input.
findings.futureDecisiveRuntime: Authorized candidate-then-late stdout/stderr and TERM-handler output cases must account every emitted byte, reap domain, and reject success at the limit; normal bounded output remains successful.
